columns.description: Leave empty. This model forecasts from the end of its fitted history
columns.name: y

assumptions: The level and the trend change by small random steps
Each driver has the same effect in all periods
avoid_when: You have many related series (this model takes one series)
The effect of a driver changes over time (the effect is the same in all periods)
data_needs: One number over time at a regular frequency
Optional drivers (for example the price). You must know their future values to forecast.
about.example: Monthly sales divide into a slow increase, a December peak and a price effect of -0.3 units for each euro.
about.expert_notes: Bayesian structural time series on pymc-extras statespace: local level, local linear or smooth trend, dummy or Fourier seasonal components (fixed or with innovations), static regression (normal or horseshoe prior; the regression states start with zero variance, so the coefficients are static). Exact Kalman likelihood (NUTS). Scores re-run a numpy Kalman filter for each kept draw: one-step-ahead inside the fit, a forecast from the terminal state after it, and a 'filter' mode that continues the fit with new data. Leave-one-out is not defined.
outputs: The level and the seasonal parts over time
The effect of each driver with a range
A filter mode that adds new periods to the fit state

references.title: Harvey (1989), Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models and the Kalman Filter
Durbin and Koopman (2012), Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods
Scott and Varian (2014), Predicting the present with Bayesian structural time series

about.summary_plain: Divides one series into a level, a trend, seasonal patterns and the effect of drivers that you know. It forecasts the series with a range of probable values.
about.title: Bayesian trend, season and drivers
use_when: You forecast one regular series and you want an honest range
The level, the trend or the seasonal pattern can change over time
Some values are missing (the model continues over the gaps)
You want to update the forecast with new periods without a new fit

manifest.description: A Bayesian structural time series: a trend, seasonal patterns and drivers, fitted with the Kalman filter of pymc-extras. Forecasts and filters start from the stored terminal state.

y_hat.description: Expected value or predictive draw: one-step-ahead inside the fitted range, a forecast after it

harmonics.description: Number of sine/cosine pairs. Empty: one effect per season (needs a whole-number period of at most 24)
harmonics.title: Harmonics

period.description: Length of the cycle in periods of the time dim (12 for monthly data with a yearly cycle, 52.18 for weekly data, 7 for daily data)
period.title: Period

sigma.description: Half-normal scale of the seasonal changes (standardised)
sigma.title: Sigma

stochastic.description: Let the seasonal pattern change over time
stochastic.title: Stochastic

initial_sd.description: Prior sd of the initial states and seasonal effects
initial_sd.title: Initial Sd

regression_prior.description: normal: every driver has an effect; horseshoe: most drivers have none
regression_prior.title: Regression Prior

regression_sigma.description: Prior scale of the driver effects (standardised)
regression_sigma.title: Regression Sigma

regressors.description: Driver variables (prices, promotions) whose future values are supplied for forecasts
regressors.title: Regressors

trend.description: level: a level that wanders; local_linear: a level and a slope that both wander; smooth: a slope that wanders slowly (a smooth trend)
trend.title: Trend

note: draws: ForecastView.total is the band of the horizon total; `level` is latent (predictive does not widen it)
